selected.text: is a wave that has come - it has no permanence and will pass. You must not allow any sadness to enter your heart and do not become sorrowful. The joy of your heart takes precedence over everything. It is not possible for worldly affairs to always accord with one's wishes
selected.reason: Acknowledges that circumstances cannot always accord with personal wishes.

selected.text: Therefore it is better that all should close their eyes to this inheritance and strive for love, affection and unity. This remains and endures, while all else is like a mirage of vain imaginings in wilderness and desert.
selected.reason: Places family affection and unity above an inheritance dispute.

selected.text: Be not sorrowful, and whenever signs of melancholy appear, occupy yourself with praises and attributes of the Ancient Beauty and the Most Great Name (may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones). Compose a lyric or ode - sorrow will be transformed to joy, grief and pain will vanish, and gladness and expansion will spread its carpet. The darkness of night will be changed to the radiance of light.
selected.reason: Proposes remembrance and praise as a spiritual practice when melancholy appears.

selected.text: until the conquering army arrived in the Holy Land and seized the reins of government for the cruel ones, and overthrew the authority of the tyrants and quietness and safety were assured. The leaders of the country and the army showed sympathy and kindness, soothing every oppressed one; the black cloud was dispersed and the horizon of the political situation cleared. Believers and unbelievers were at rest, and acquaintances and strangers were playing cheerful melodies.
selected.reason: A specific historical ending of tyranny supplies an instance of relief after fear.

selected.text: thou must constantly provide means for her joy and gladness, that she may find at least some measure of solace and her heartfelt grief may be somewhat alleviated. By God! To gladden her heart is to bring joy to the hearts of the Concourse of the All-Glorious, and to comfort her is to comfort the denizens of the Supreme Concourse.
selected.reason: Requires continuing practical efforts to alleviate grief, even when only partial solace is possible.

selected.text: O Lord! Calm his anxiety and disturbance, and grant rest to his spirit through the breezes of pardon and forgiveness and the melodies of the birds of the garden of bounty, and forgive the sins.
selected.reason: Prayer asks directly for the calming of anxiety and disturbance.

selected.text: Though the sighs ye have uttered and your lamentation have been silent and concealed, yet in truth they are clearly heard by the denizens of the heavens. The Concourse on High hath attentive ears and the eyes of God are all-seeing. They perceive everything. Know thou that that entreaties of the faithful at the threshold of His singleness are answered and their desires granted, but owing to His inscrutable wisdom, all things are contingent upon time and await the appointed hour.
selected.reason: Recognizes concealed suffering and explains that relief may depend on time.

selected.text: Night and day supplications ascend to the Most Exalted Horizon that means may be provided for some comfort and ease to be arranged for your honor. … Although in this elemental world ease is neither possible nor attainable, yet the degree of difficulties can vary
selected.reason: Distinguishes the absence of perfect ease from meaningful reductions in difficulty.

selected.text: My hope is that such a precious soul may day by day increase in honor and prosperity and become the cause of lightening the afflictions of Iran and the Iranians.
selected.reason: Invites a person’s prosperity to become a means of relieving the suffering of others.

selected.text: Those regions are in great need of divine glad tidings, for all have become despondent and dejected from the severity of the afflictions of war. They are dead and withered, in need of the breath of life, and the breath of life is the glad tidings of the Kingdom. Nothing will deliver them from this grief and sorrow and dejection and hopelessness except the divine glad tidings.
selected.reason: Addresses the collective despondency left by war, extending consolation beyond individual grief.

selected.text: He expressed the utmost gratitude for your efforts. This nursing was service to God, and this kindness arose from the requirements of servitude at the Sacred Threshold. Your troubles and hardships are accepted at the Divine Threshold, and your love and kindness are praised and approved in the Abha Kingdom.
selected.reason: Explicitly praises nursing and caregiving as service to God.

selected.text: Think not that you have been forgotten. You are ever before my sight, your services and endeavors are before my eyes, your trials and tribulations and hardships are in my thoughts, and your wandering and estrangement are clear and evident. Therefore I beseech God for confirmation, that He may become your Helper and Protector, your Supporter and Aid, so that, God willing, you may spend your remaining days in comfort and ease
selected.reason: Recognizes past service and suffering and wishes for comfort in remaining years.

selected.text: Despite this, I beseech God to make the friends prosperous and flourishing in every way, to grant them stability, to bestow flowing treasures, and to make them manifestations of "Grant us good in this world and good in the world to come." May these breaches be repaired and these rents be mended. Be confident.
selected.reason: Prays for material stability, prosperity and the repair of losses.

selected.text: Praise be to God, this servant's entreaties and supplications reached the threshold of the Divine Unity, and after the darkness of tribulation, the dawn of hope appeared, and some measure of relief was obtained by you.
selected.reason: Records some actual relief after tribulation, complementing passages about future hope.

selected.text: In truth, when I imagine the difficulties and tribulations and trials and pains and exile and distress of that blessed leaf, the utmost grief and sorrow results. But O pure leaf, do not be sorrowful … Soon thou shalt behold with grateful eyes the rewards of these hardships and the benefits of these difficulties. Thou art under the eye of His grace and included in the confirmations of His mercy. Be confident and take thy rest
selected.reason: Names the consoler’s grief at another person’s exile and invites the recipient to rest.

selected.text: I am your companion and your intimate friend. Why then do you grieve when you have one like 'Abdu'l-Baha to share your sorrows? At every moment I think of you and at every instant I mention you at the Threshold of the Most Great Name.
selected.reason: Presents companionship as sharing another person’s sorrows.

selected.text: Let me know if thou shouldst desire anyone from here to come to thee, that I may send the person along -- even Munirih -- so that thou wilt not be homesick. … That thou shouldst spend a few days of peace and rest, is my dearest wish
selected.reason: Offers to send a chosen companion to relieve homesickness and seeks days of peace and rest.

selected.text: O Lord! He is broken before Thee - mend his brokenness, expand his straitened circumstances, enlarge his breast, make his affairs easy
selected.reason: Prayer joins mending brokenness with improving straitened circumstances and easing affairs.

selected.text: Therefore there must be intense hope and firm expectation, for He is the shelter of sinners and the refuge of the erring ones … Therefore we must be confident in the grace and bounty of the Sovereign of existence
selected.reason: Grounds hope in divine mercy toward people who have erred.

selected.text: Although these are cruel times and you have been unemployed for some days, yet be hopeful, for this is in the path of the Lord. Be not sorrowful, for hardship does not endure
selected.reason: Addresses unemployment in difficult times as a concrete occasion for hope.

selected.text: O my physician, O my beloved! I have grieved at your intense sorrow and yearned for you as a bird in exile yearns for its happy mate. I wished to console you in this fresh affliction, this grievous calamity and great bereavement.
selected.reason: Offers intimate consolation to a physician experiencing bereavement.

selected.text: O thou who art attracted by the fragrances of God! Thy recent letter hath been received and I have read its wondrous contents. We have sent thee a reply by telegraph concerning the command to depart. And as for thee, O precious handmaiden of God, be thou assured of healing from every ailment through the power of the Spirit from God. At that time, the clouds of tests shall be dispersed, revealing a light shining brilliantly throughout all existence. These tempests shall pass away and the radiant light shall appear, and thy heart shall find tranquillity through the outpouring of thy Lord's tender mercies, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate
selected.reason: A reply sent by telegram illustrates prompt personal reassurance across distance.

selected.text: You too must inevitably have your share and portion of this, for true faithfulness demands that one be a partner and participant in both joy and sorrow, comfort and hardship, glory and abasement.
selected.reason: Describes faithfulness as sharing both comfort and hardship, joy and sorrow.

selected.text: O Afnan of the Blessed Tree! It would be good if his father would make an effort in this matter so that reconciliation may be achieved between that son and father
selected.reason: Calls for effort toward reconciliation between a father and son.

selected.text: Bestow upon us a cure from the dispensary of Thy mercy, and grant us a healing balm from Thy supreme panacea, that these broken hearts may find solace, and these withered and dejected souls may find rest and gladness. May this night of sorrows be followed by a bright morn, and may this deadly poison be sweetened by wondrous honey.
selected.reason: Prayer develops healing imagery for broken hearts without erasing their pain.

selected.text: Sorrow not because of thy poverty for thou shalt attain all dignity, nor be grieved for thy destitution for thou shalt obtain true wealth. Do not dwell on thy humiliation for thou shalt be confirmed and assisted from on high.
selected.reason: Separates human dignity from poverty, destitution and humiliation.

selected.text: O my Lord! Perfume the nostrils of Thy servant who is bound in chains with the fragrances of Thy holiness in every morn and eve, and illumine his sight with beholding the lights of Thy grace at every dawn and dusk, that it may be a solace to him in his constraints and prison, and a companion in his loneliness.
selected.reason: Prayer seeks companionship and consolation for a person bound in prison.

selected.text: One must look at matters with the eye of wisdom and consider with thought and reflection … Now whatever befalls you, remembrance of what has passed brings consolation to the heart, and engagement in teaching causes expansion of the breast
selected.reason: Connects comfort with thoughtful reflection on past events and purposeful activity.

selected.text: Some thoughts come to your mind which make you very sad, but do not let anything make you sad and do not let things of this world attract you. Sometimes you feel that your friends are faithless, but remember that God is a friend that can be relied upon and He is faithful and true, and He alone is to be implicitly trusted.
selected.reason: Reported counsel addresses sorrowful thoughts and the question of whom to trust.

selected.text: If you have a bed of lilies-of-the-valley that you love and tenderly care for, they cannot see you, nor can they understand your care, nevertheless, because of that tender care, they flourish. … So it is with your husband. You cannot see him, but his loving influence surrounds you, cares for you, watches over you
selected.reason: A reported image of cared-for lilies explores loving influence that cannot be directly seen.

selected.text: A cheerful countenance lends consolation to the beholder.
selected.reason: A reported saying names a cheerful countenance as a simple way to console others.

selected.text: by virtue of "souls are like recruited troops" I have found the cord of love connected
selected.reason: The Bab’s image of a connected cord of love expands the theme of companionship.

selected.text: Let them not be disheartened. This condition has ever appeared in times of Manifestation. According to what is recorded, four hundred souls subsisted on dates for several days during the time of the Seal of the Prophets, may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for His sake. This poverty is the owner of wealth, for it is for God and in God's path.
selected.reason: Historical shared poverty provides a concrete religious precedent rather than an abstract assurance.

selected.text: O Muhammad-'Ali! Grieve not over anything. The sorrow and joy of the world are both transient. God willing, thou shalt be confirmed in that which altereth not and shall not be erased from the scroll of names.
selected.reason: Emphasizes the transience of both joy and sorrow, inviting an even-handed perspective.

selected.text: O My loved ones! Let not exile grieve you. Whosoever seeketh Me, in whatsoever land he may be, verily dwelleth in the homeland of the All-Merciful.
selected.reason: Reframes homeland for people in exile through their relationship with God.

selected.text: I bear witness by My Most Exalted Pen, My Most Glorious Countenance, My Most Sweet Utterance, and all that is attributed to God, the Lord of Names, that I have never rejected thee for a single moment, nor have My care and kindness towards thee ever changed, nor hath My heart and soul ever been troubled by thee.
selected.reason: Assures a recipient that affection and acceptance have not changed.

selected.text: O people of God! Be not grieved. Ere long will God, exalted be His glory, adorn the embodiments of oppression with the raiment of justice and the temples of tyranny with the ornament of equity.
selected.reason: Hopes for oppressors themselves to adopt justice and equity.

selected.text: And verily, He shall be with thee in thy solitude, and in the hour when thou enterest a place wherein there is neither lamp, nor bed, nor helper, nor assistant. And He shall be with thee and shall not part from thee in thy exile and thy solitude.
selected.reason: Promises companionship in utter solitude without ordinary material supports.

selected.text: We were verily with thee in thy departure and arrival, and in thy bewilderment and grief, and We witnessed thy condition. Therefore, grieve not within thyself, but be joyous through the loving-kindness of thy Lord.
selected.reason: Acknowledges a person’s departure, arrival, bewilderment and grief as individually witnessed.

selected.text: And if the fulfillment of certain wishes of the friends be delayed, they should not become sorrowful. … Fix thy gaze upon this blessed word which, like unto the sun, hath shone forth from the horizon of the divine Tablet and was sent to one of the servants: The pulse of the world is in the hand of the skilled Physician. He perceiveth the disease and in His wisdom prescribeth the remedy
selected.reason: Qualifies delayed wishes through the image of the wise physician and appropriate remedy.

selected.text: It is submitted that your grief and sorrow has not become so manifest as to eliminate or remove your loving correspondence and affectionate communications.
selected.reason: Encourages loving correspondence to continue despite grief.

selected.text: We beseech God, glorified and mighty be He, to assuage with the waters of patience the ardor in the hearts of them that are sincere, which hath been kindled by manifest tribulations.
selected.reason: Prayer images patience as cooling water for hearts inflamed by tribulation.

selected.text: I beseech Thee, O our Lord, the All-Merciful, by Thy Name which dominateth over the worlds and transcendeth all possibility, to draw her near unto Thee in every world of Thy worlds and to ordain for her that which shall solace her eyes and tranquilize her soul.
selected.reason: Prayer asks for nearness, solace and tranquility for a particular woman.

selected.text: Thou must at all times drink from the chalice of joy and gladness, for that which came upon you in the path of God caused the Concourse on High to weep and lament.
selected.reason: Joins an invitation to joy with explicit heavenly weeping over the recipient’s suffering.

selected.text: We make mention of Our tribulations in measure, lest grief overtake Our loved ones in hardships and trials. He, verily, is the Helper, the All-Wise.
selected.reason: Explains measured disclosure of suffering as care against overwhelming loved ones.

selected.text: of God. However, in this Revelation all are commanded to observe wisdom. Therefore no action contrary to wisdom should be manifested. Be not thou distressed over any matter. God willing, thou hast been and wilt continue to be beneath the shadow of divine favor
selected.reason: Makes observance of wisdom an explicit condition alongside spiritual reassurance.

selected.text: Do not grieve over what was mentioned regarding the pitcher. Verily your Lord is the Great Ocean.
selected.reason: The pitcher and ocean image offers a distinctive response to a concrete concern.

selected.text: We have heard that thy son hath ascended unto God. We share in thy sorrow and beseech God to cause him to dwell nigh unto His mercy, to give him to drink from the cups of His bounty, to purify him from transgression and clothe him in the robes of forgiveness - verily He is the Most Merciful of the merciful - and to place him in the highest companionship, in fellowship with His chosen ones and loved ones, and to send down upon him at every moment a mercy from His presence. Verily He is the All-Bountiful, the Ancient of Days. But grieve thou not. By God! If thou wert to look with the eye of the heart, thou wouldst behold him even now freed from all opposition, detached from those who disbelieved and associated partners with God, and in communion with those on whose faces thou findest the freshness of bliss.
selected.reason: Shares a parent’s sorrow and prays for the deceased son’s nearness to mercy.

selected.text: Had He not been with you, you would not have attained to His recognition nor would you have been speaking His praise. Since He is with you, all existence is with you.
selected.reason: Develops recognition and remembrance as evidence of divine companionship.

selected.text: We make mention of Our tribulations lest those who have believed should grieve at what hath touched them in My path … We console him who hath borne tribulation and give him glad tidings of a noble station
selected.reason: Explains how recounting shared tribulations can itself console those who suffer.

selected.text: Verily the Wronged One remembereth every wronged man and woman, and the Stranger loveth every stranger, man and woman, and every captive man and woman, especially those who are made such in the path of God.
selected.reason: Extends remembrance and love to wronged people, strangers and captives, both men and women.

selected.text: Some of the friends in that land, due to hardship and difficulty, are in need of solace. Be thou a comforter on behalf of this Prisoner.
selected.reason: Entrusts a person with consoling others on behalf of the imprisoned writer.

selected.text: Your letter was received. Its perusal conveyed the utmost supplication and communion. Your lamentation and cries, in reality effect the hearts, especially the heart of 'Abduil-Baha. If you could realize what an effect your letter produced, undoubtedly you would feel assured that the heart of 'Abduil-Baha has the utmost attachment to you, and day and night he is supplicating toward the Kingdom of Abha and begs for you confirmation
selected.reason: Acknowledges that another person’s lamentation moves the consoler’s heart.

selected.text: As much as you can, strengthen your heart and turn with intensity to the Divine - what is broken shall be mended. After clouds come rain, and after rain comes sunshine. Treasure is found in ruins, and stars shine brightest at night.
selected.reason: Develops the hope of mending what is broken through images of changing weather and hidden treasure.

selected.text: To his honor Aqa Abdul-Husayn, convey this servant's utmost satisfaction with his efforts … These services were for the Truth, not for him, and are accounted with God
selected.reason: Affirms the value of service even when its human recipient is disappointing.

selected.text: I hope you will be enabled to act according to this blessed verse which states: "Give glad tidings to the patient ones, who when afflicted with calamity say: 'Verily we are God's, and verily unto Him shall we return
selected.reason: Connects consolation with the Quranic return-to-God formula and glad tidings to the patient.

selected.text: Therefore comfort your heart and submit to the decree of the Generous Lord … show her the utmost consideration and respect, protect her rights, and treat her beyond what she deserves so that poor woman may find solace in this great calamity
selected.reason: Requires consideration, respect and protection of a bereaved woman’s rights.

selected.text: O Lord! Rashid Keykhosrow has taken refuge at Thy gate and sought shelter at Thy Most Exalted Threshold. He was fearful and afraid because of sin and transgression, and weak and helpless from tribulations. Grant him a gift, bestow forgiveness, pardon his sins, give him refuge and shelter
selected.reason: Prayer addresses fear arising from wrongdoing with forgiveness, refuge and shelter.

selected.text: Though thy kith and kin have cast thee out from among them, in reality thou art the sole one among thy relatives to be a loved and honoured servant of God. This is the bountiful recompense for the torments thou hast suffered and the good reward for all the pain thou hast endured. Grieve not nor begrudge them anything and do not grow bitter, for after some time those very souls who have rejected thee will reclaim their relationship with thee and even thine enemies will noise abroad their friendship with thee and their love how much more thy kith and kin. This cruelty will come to kindness in the end and these bitter dregs will be transformed to the pure crystalline stream from which thou shalt assuredly drink.
selected.reason: Consoles a person expelled by relatives while affirming their dignity.

selected.text: O divine captives! Let it not cross your mind for a moment that those prisoners in the path of God have been forgotten or neglected, or that they are deprived of the attention of hearts
selected.reason: Assures prisoners that they remain in the attention and affection of others.

selected.text: Do not be sorrowful, do not be grieved. 'Abdu'l-Baha, with tearful eyes, begs forgiveness and pardon for him. … Tell the divine friends never to be sorrowful for those who ascend
selected.reason: Places tearful prayer beside counsel against sorrow, an important nuance in the treatment of grief.

selected.text: Although this is a state to be envied and desired, you are compelled to remain in order to protect the young children and attend to affairs. Therefore, I beseech the Court of Oneness that the reward of pilgrimage be ordained for you and that you may be blessed with this supreme honor in the future.
selected.reason: Makes care and protection of young children a concrete reason to remain and attend to responsibilities.

selected.text: His honor Mishkin-Qalam, whenever he becomes downhearted, remembers you and involuntarily, like an overflowing cup, becomes the cause of happiness and joy of the righteous ones, and never forgets you, and always at the Sacred Threshold begs confirmation for
selected.reason: Remembrance of a friend transforms one person’s sadness and spreads joy to others.

selected.text: O ye refugees of the one true God! Be not grieved or disconsolate; neither allow yourselves to sit despondent and dejected. Though you have been persecuted, made homeless, and humiliated, this was in the path of that loving Friend, Who was Himself exiled from Iran to Iraq, from Iraq to the Great City (Constantinople), from thence to Rumelia (Adrianople), and from Rumelia to this afflictive prison. You have followed in His
selected.reason: Addresses displaced refugees in their actual experience of persecution and exile.

selected.text: yet since the descent of this greatest calamity is assuredly based on the Most Great Wisdom … If you were aware of this mystery, you would surely not have begun to cry out and lament in grief. But though my eyes weep, it is from the tenderness of heart and delicacy of feeling
selected.reason: Explains the writer’s own tears through tenderness and feeling rather than absence of hope.

selected.text: your letter arrived and your cry and lamentation was heard. It caused great astonishment that due to hardship you wished to depart from this world, and especially that you desire the destruction of your lineage and family. What an empty thought this is and what an unsuitable intention
selected.reason: Responds to a recipient’s wish to die because of hardship, requiring its full personal context and life-affirming counsel.

selected.text: The matter of your company's losses caused grief and sorrow, but do not be sorrowful, perhaps God will bring about something after this.
selected.reason: Recognizes sorrow over business losses as a concrete form of distress.

selected.text: Grant refuge and shelter to the helpless and wandering ones … Be their helper and protector so that every captive and poor one may receive a portion and share from Thy table of bounties
selected.reason: Prayer seeks refuge, protection and a share of material bounty for helpless, wandering and poor people.

selected.text: You had complained about visits and meetings with friends and strangers. Thus it became clear that rest is impossible and unattainable for man - either he is afflicted by the onslaught and torment of strangers, or he is troubled by the comings and goings of the heedless. In either case, weariness and melancholy are present and ready.
selected.reason: Acknowledges that both solitude and excessive visits can bring weariness, qualifying simple assumptions about comfort.

selected.text: I am truly very ashamed before you, that circumstances conspired such that you could not rest for a moment nor find peace for an instant … However, you had an agreeable companion, so no harm was done - compensation was achieved
selected.reason: The writer acknowledges a guest’s lack of rest and values an agreeable companion.

selected.text: Remember those days when in Iraq we reclined in the shade of the Tree of Providence, and in every hour through increased favors and bounties we reached the utmost of our desires. Remember those bright nights and those times like rose gardens and flower beds that passed.
selected.reason: Recollection of shared days provides a concrete form of consolation through memory.

selected.text: This servant is occupied day and night in remembrance of those noble ones, and has not had nor has a moment's separation. … All the friends must circle like moths around those two wronged candles with wisdom
selected.reason: Directs the community to surround suffering people with care while observing wisdom.

selected.text: For now, travel to Tehran is better - there thou wilt be more at peace and perhaps some occupation may also be found, so that thou mayest pass some days under the shadow of grace. Be confident that great gifts are destined and mighty favors are assured.
selected.reason: Proposes travel to a safer place with possible employment as practical relief.

selected.text: Therefore he should not be affected, for the fame of his truthfulness, trustworthiness and capability has reached even to the Holy Shrine … they should not be sad and sorrowful. In this transient world no matter continues permanently. Sometimes there is dismissal and sometimes appointment, sometimes there is success and sometimes lack of joy
selected.reason: Affirms trustworthiness despite disappointment and recognizes alternating success and difficulty.

selected.text: Trust thou in the favor of thy Master and be not saddened by anything. In all affairs be thou patient, dignified, thankful, calm, kind, tender, tolerant, self-restrained; for this is the quality of the near ones.
selected.reason: Brings patience together with dignity, kindness, tenderness, tolerance and self-restraint.

selected.text: God willing, hereafter may all news in all directions be the cause of joy for all, meaning may events that cause sorrow cease.
selected.reason: Explicitly wishes for sorrow-causing events themselves to cease.

selected.text: If ye have written letters to Abdul-Baha and answers to them are delayed, know ye of a certainty that untold hindrances have been the cause. Be ye not unhappy … Should ye send a hundred letters and no answers be received, do ye not feel at all sad
selected.reason: Explains delayed replies without making unanswered correspondence a sign of rejection.

selected.text: Be assured. … Nevertheless, I am not content with your hardship. I would not trade a single hair of yours for a thousand gardens
selected.reason: Expressly refuses to be content with another person’s hardship, an essential qualification.

selected.text: console him every hour so that his heart may find rest
selected.reason: Calls for repeated, attentive consolation rather than a single expression of sympathy.

selected.text: Become a balm for souls and healing for aching hearts.
selected.reason: Invites people themselves to become healing for aching hearts.

selected.text: But as we know these cages all of them will be broken at the end and the imprisoned birds will fly to the heaven of mysteries. They will have their nest under the shade of the tree of holiness and this separation will have such reunion at its end and this solitude will have such a fragrant joy at the end that you should not ever be sad. Its separation will not last. Alienation and remotness will be eliminated. … We all hope and trust that all of us will be gathered together in the centre of beauty, the world of glory, kingdom of light and the assemblage of reunion
selected.reason: Develops the image of birds released from cages and reunion in the spiritual world.

selected.text: Days will come when you will forget all these things and divine glad tidings will so encompass you that you will seek forgiveness and pardon for those cruel ones and treat them with the utmost kindness. These bitter days, more bitter than poison, shall pass away; Once again days sweet as sugar shall return.
selected.reason: Looks toward forgiveness for those who caused suffering as grief is transformed.

selected.text: His Holiness Joseph was in the land of Egypt and His Holiness Jacob in the land of Canaan, yet despite this great distance, the fragrance of Joseph's garment was perceived. In any case, give thanks to God that though absent you are present, and gazing toward the highest horizon.
selected.reason: Uses Joseph and Jacob to explore spiritual nearness across geographical separation.

selected.text: Do not be sorrowful and grieved by the great calamities that have befallen you. Every breast is a target for the arrow of tribulation, and every heart is afflicted with some sorrow
selected.reason: Acknowledges that every heart bears some sorrow, connecting personal suffering with shared humanity.

selected.text: Although the means of comfort and ease never became available to you, and I know that you are under hardship and difficulty, nevertheless you have served at the Sacred Threshold and this is the greatest glad tidings and joy - it is the heart's desire and the soul's comfort
selected.reason: Recognizes meaningful service even when hoped-for material comfort never became available.

selected.text: This separation was the essence of union, and this parting caused the stirring of conscience. This very longing and emotion is a bounty, and its influence brings forth grace and favor.
selected.reason: Explores longing and emotional connection as potentially fruitful rather than merely deficient.

selected.text: Do not thou be grieved because of the loss of thy sight. Praise be unto God, that thy insight is keen. Do not thou lament over thy poverty, for the Treasury of the Kingdom is thine. Do not thou worry that thou couldst not study in the material schools, because thou hast received lessons in the Verses of the Oneness (of God) in the Divine University.
selected.reason: Distinguishes loss of physical sight and material poverty from spiritual insight and worth.

selected.text: Although this calamity was so grievous that a mountain of iron would not have strength and patience to endure it, nor would the mightiest structure be able to withstand it, yet is the wisdom of the All-Glorious Lord hidden and concealed.
selected.reason: Acknowledges a calamity beyond ordinary endurance while leaving divine wisdom hidden.

selected.text: I am very sad that I cannot provide new assistance, and whenever possible, you know that I will not fall short. … Thus, I write this letter with utmost embarrassment and hope from God's favors that means of comfort will be provided for you
selected.reason: Candidly states the inability to provide new material assistance while affirming willingness to help when possible.

selected.text: The effort you made in paying the debt of Bashir-i-Ilahi was a distinguished service, accepted and evident at the Divine Threshold.
selected.reason: Praises paying another person’s debt as a concrete service.

selected.text: Praise be to God that this interpreter is between us; therefore be thou not sad
selected.reason: The presence of an interpreter overcomes a barrier to communication and companionship.

selected.text: Soon they will completely pass away. Be confident, and if continuing to stay in that land becomes very difficult and you must go to a place of refuge, that too is permitted.
selected.reason: Explicitly permits seeking refuge elsewhere if remaining becomes too difficult.

selected.text: the Blessed Shrine in these days presents many obstacles. On behalf of both him and you, I turn toward the Sacred Dust and perform the visitation
selected.reason: Offers to perform visitation for people prevented from reaching the shrine.

selected.text: Praise be to God that the wound has healed, and through the efforts of the honorable Consul and respected individuals, a remedy was found.
selected.reason: Recognizes actual remedy obtained through the efforts of a consul and other people.

selected.text: If in this mortal world some hardship befalls, praise be to God in the divine world there is abundant and pre-existing mercy. If people have turned away from you, praise be to God the glances of the eye of the All-Merciful encompass you and grace and mercy are complete. … This is sufficient, and all else is pure delusion and like tales and stories. Be confident and joyous and delighted by the grace and favor of the Intended Lord
selected.reason: Responds to rejection by others through divine grace and belonging.

selected.text: Do not become melancholy and sorrowful from the difficulties, calamities and hardships in this world, for every condition passes away and ultimately proves fruitless and without result. Every comfort vanishes and every trouble and hardship comes to an end.
selected.reason: Treats comfort and hardship alike as changing circumstances.

selected.text: Therefore, a letter of consolation was written and is enclosed with this letter. You should also write a letter of consolation and sympathy and place this letter inside it and send it.

selected.text: Be thou sure that, verily, thy deceased child is now one of those babes who are suckled in the Kingdom of Life, under the charge of the Beauty of El-ABHA

selected.text: You are a source of solace for hearts, not trouble for souls

selected.text: Therefore do not be sorrowful or grieved at his passing, for human life is through the soul, not the body - through the spirit, not the pain-filled form.

selected.text: He is in distress - grant him rest and comfort. He is destitute - make him prosperous. He is powerless - make him able
selected.reason: Prayer joins comfort with prosperity for the destitute and ability for the powerless.

selected.reason: Connects joy with friendship and kindness toward every people and nation.

selected.text: Be thou patient with their defections, and exercise thou toward them the utmost kindness. Look thou not upon their errors
selected.reason: Counsels patience and kindness toward others despite their failings.

selected.reason: Uses the suffering of holy figures to question comfort as the sole measure of a good life.

selected.text: I love you tenderly and I knew that you are drinking deep of the cup of afflictions … I love you tenderly, very tenderly, and you are always to find comfort in this thought
selected.reason: Repeated personal assurance of tender love directly addresses someone deeply afflicted.

selected.reason: Connects remembrance of the deceased with the ethical conduct of survivors.

selected.text: be thou not unhappy … Be thou not sad. This indifference is temporary

selected.reason: Uses the Quranic image of martyrs living with their Lord as a distinct basis for consolation.

selected.reason: Recognizes that continued employment would have been beneficial while seeking peace after its loss.

selected.text: Regarding thy extreme sorrow, thy sadness and thy great regret for My imprisonment, there is no harm therein.
selected.reason: States that sorrow over the writer’s imprisonment is not in itself wrong.

selected.reason: Personal counsel on marital distress turns toward companionship in the community; its specific setting must remain clear.

selected.reason: Corrects an unofficial personal claim that had threatened the recipient’s assurance.

selected.reason: The rose and rose-water image explores what remains after loss.

selected.reason: A cited Persian poem offers consolation through the passing of bitter days.

selected.text: Since the handmaid of Baha, the wife of the martyr who is departing, hath endured severe trials in the path of God, therefore the utmost consideration must be shown toward her.

selected.text: It is difficult for the weak ones to endure the tests but for souls like you, it is very easy.
selected.reason: Distinguishes people’s capacity to endure tests, to be read with passages acknowledging overwhelming loss.

selected.reason: Invites temporary separation to produce tenderness rather than only distress.

selected.reason: Distinguishes the grief of survivors from the spiritual state attributed to the deceased.

selected.reason: Describes obtaining some solace while grief remains, avoiding an all-or-nothing account of consolation.

selected.text: Do not become sorrowful, disappointed and distracted by the objection and insult of the heedless teacher.

selected.text: Praise be to God that the regions of Iran are safe and secure, and the just government has raised its tent, protecting and preserving all.

selected.text: The children of that deceased one are my children. All must show them the utmost consideration on my behalf so that they do not think they are orphans.

selected.text: be patient for now and think about your own comfort and happiness until he returns from Europe

selected.reason: Reported wartime counsel considers children bereaved of a parent and faith as a source of support.

selected.reason: Reported words connect mutual harmony and universal care with consolation for the speaker.

selected.text: The greatest consolation for the heart is the Love of God. This is the balm for every wound and the remedy for every ailment. This world is full of pain and afflictions. Therefore the foundation upon which the eternal consolation of the human heart is based
selected.reason: A reported statement identifies the love of God as the foundation of lasting consolation.

selected.text: The best man is that person who cheers and gladdens the broken-hearted ones and the worst man is that soul who causes suffering and pain to one's heart. Consequently strive as much s you are able to rejoice the hearts and uplifts the spirits
selected.reason: A reported ethical contrast places cheering broken hearts against causing others pain.

selected.reason: The Bab explicitly shares a correspondent’s sorrow before turning to contentment.

selected.reason: The Bab’s correspondence includes family reassurance and a concrete choice about where to stay.

selected.reason: The Bab counsels against dwelling excessively on grief while maintaining hope and patience.

selected.reason: Records another person’s tears on hearing of the recipient’s troubles, preserving shared feeling.

selected.reason: Recalls relief arriving in situations where ordinary hope had been cut off.

selected.reason: Prayer seeks inward tranquility and patience together with deeper understanding.

selected.reason: Presents the divine word as planting hope in human hearts.

selected.text: Be not grieved. The host of the servant is resignation and prayer. … In all conditions, I beseech and implore the Blessed and Exalted Lord to refresh your honor with the rain of His mercy and grace, and to ordain for you the good of this world and the next
selected.reason: Pairs resignation with active prayer for good in this world and the next.

selected.reason: Admits that separation still causes real pain despite earlier arguments about its spiritual value.

selected.reason: Prayer joins reunion of scattered loved ones with protection and justice against those who separated them.

selected.text: We console thy mother with God's mercy and His favors, and We make mention of her in this noble station. She hath been immersed in tribulations which none knoweth save the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. She must not grieve over what hath befallen her.
selected.reason: Acknowledges a mother’s troubles as deeper than other people can fully know.

selected.reason: Affirms prior and continuing love through several layers of witness.

selected.reason: Connects written remembrance with enduring companionship beyond present circumstances.

selected.reason: Directly replaces a despairing self-description with one of assurance in divine care.

selected.reason: Links reassurance and gratitude with learning the ways of wisdom.

selected.reason: Acknowledges that outward events did not fulfill the recipient’s wish.

selected.reason: Explains beautiful patience through the impermanence of worldly events.

selected.reason: The writer describes personal contentment and praise despite distress.

selected.reason: Combines patience and reliance with bringing anguish and grief to God.

selected.text: Grieve not over anything or anyone. By the life of God, I am with thee, I am thy companion, thy protector and thy helper
selected.reason: Names companionship, protection and assistance together as forms of divine support.

selected.reason: Offers reading morning and evening as a concrete practice for the pain of separation.

selected.reason: Invites reflection on the divine name Self-Subsisting as a theological source of assurance.

selected.reason: Describes the community’s tears joining the recipient’s tears.

selected.reason: Recalls a particular experience of preservation in prison, grounding consolation in remembered events.

selected.reason: The actual preparation of tablets and mention of names give personal remembrance a concrete setting.

selected.text: Be not grieved by what hath befallen thee, for thou art unaware of the ultimate outcome of things. "It may be that you hate a thing which is good for you."
selected.reason: Acknowledges ignorance of ultimate outcomes and cites the possibility of good in what is disliked.

selected.text: Thy compositions are indeed the most great remedy for the sorrows of the world, and each one, corresponding to a different clime, brought joy to many who perused it. They have been and ever shall be a source of eternal gladness.
selected.reason: Praises compositions that console people in different regions, identifying an artistic contribution to comfort.

selected.text: Be not saddened by the differences in newly-arisen matters in the world. For every matter there is a time. When it cometh to pass it shall appear as God, the Sovereign, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, hath willed.
selected.reason: States that newly arising matters each have their time, qualifying immediate expectations.

selected.text: Be not grieved at anything. We beseech God to make the crescent moon of thy hope into a full moon, and the star of thy desire into a radiant sun.
selected.reason: The crescent-to-full-moon image develops the growth of hope.

selected.text: Verily, We love him and beseech God to assist him with the hosts of the unseen and the visible world.
selected.reason: Asks for assistance through both visible and unseen means.

selected.text: Pay them no attention, give them no importance, show no disturbance. Be forbearing, let it pass with a smile
selected.reason: Forbearance and a measured response to provocation give a practical discipline of consolation.

selected.text: God be praised, thou hast a kind Lord Who healeth every sick one and dispelleth the sorrow of every afflicted soul. He is a shelter to the orphan and a helper of the destitute, and His kindness knoweth no bounds.
selected.reason: Names healing, shelter for orphans and help for the destitute as forms of divine kindness.

selected.text: Do not begin to wail over the ascension of that pure leaf, and do not weep and lament. Do not be sorrowful, do not be grief-stricken, do not beat your breast, do not scratch your face, do not rend your collar
selected.reason: Addresses particular bodily mourning practices; retain its personal setting and distinguish comfort from denying grief.

selected.reason: Adds the Bab's treatment of mortality, patience and return to God, including the surrounding poetic unit.

selected.reason: Preserves this exact version of an important distinction between bodily ease and contentment amid persecution.

selected.reason: Distinguishes visible composure from hidden disorder and pairs that admission with hope of practical improvement.

selected.reason: Offers the distinctive and potentially challenging idea of consolation through shared general hardship.

selected.text: Therefore, you must exercise patience and forbearance, and not give way to lamentation and anxiety in this calamity. selected.reason: States the relationship between patience, complaint and unavoidable events through an explicitly attributed saying.

selected.text: I hope that your end may be a good one and that the means of ease, comfort and happiness may be provided, although comfort and ease are impossible in this world.
selected.reason: Holds a wish for actual relief together with the limits of lasting worldly ease.

selected.text: Both dreams are evidence that thou art regarded with the glance of favor and art near to the Divine Threshold, and through abundant grace art protected and joyous in the shelter of the All-Forgiving Lord
selected.reason: Preserves an individual dream response as a personal form of assurance, without making it a universal interpretive rule.

selected.text: Ask after that poor sister who left that house with several ailments and has settled in the utmost joy, tranquility and dignity in the home of His Honor Kalim, and by God's grace is in perfect comfort
selected.reason: Calls for follow-up care of a sick woman who has found dignified refuge in another household.

selected.text: Grieve not in hardship nor rejoice in ease, for with every hardship comes ease and with every ease comes hardship. Both shall pass away and perish.
selected.reason: Extends equanimity to both hardship and ease, grounding comfort in their shared impermanence.

selected.reason: Assures a separated handmaiden that service and divine presence are not confined to one geographical place.

selected.text: Be ye not saddened by frozen hearts. The cause of their prevention hath been this ephemeral world, and God is powerful over its transformation.
selected.reason: Grounds hope for hardened hearts in the possibility of their transformation.

selected.text: There hath come upon Us from him whom We sheltered for numbered years that which hath caused all things to lament and raised the crying of earth and heaven. Thus hath the matter been decreed from before God, the Commander, the All-Wise.
selected.reason: Acknowledges the sorrow of betrayal by someone formerly sheltered and cared for.

selected.text: He verily fulfilleth what hath been promised in the Book. Let nothing sadden thee. She verily ascended to God and returned to Him just as she had appeared from Him. She hath returned, rested, rejoiced and is overjoyed.
selected.reason: Expresses consolation after a woman's death through return to God and fulfilment of divine promise.

selected.text: O 'Ali! We have heard of thy arrival in prison and make mention of thee, that thy heart may rejoice
selected.reason: Records a direct act of remembrance when a named recipient has newly entered prison.

selected.text: By the life of our Purpose! The angels of heaven are grieved and saddened by the oppression that hath been wrought. This is what my Lord, the All-Hearing, hath informed Me. I beseech Him, exalted be He, to aid you, to grant you success, to protect you from the evil of His enemies, and to seize those who have denied His right, broken His covenant, and committed that which hath caused every fair-minded and discerning one to lament.
selected.reason: Affirms moral grief at oppression, balancing injunctions to patience with lament for injustice.

selected.text: and favor he hath now freed and liberated himself from the ocean of oppression and corruption. Therefore We seek his contentment, that he be not troubled, for from the earliest days he had shown love towards Us. We have loved and continue to love faithfulness
selected.reason: Addresses comfort after escape from oppression and explicitly values long-standing faithfulness.

selected.text: Despair not of the Spirit of God. He is with thee and with those who are round about thee. Remind them of the wonders of My remembrance, that they may rejoice in the glad-tidings of God, the King, the Mighty, the All-Knowing.
selected.reason: Invites the recipient to extend remembered glad tidings to the surrounding community.

selected.text: In brief, there is no rest for man in this world; you cannot find a soul who has no grief or sorrow. However, if one has spiritual sensibilities, if one's attention is directed to the divine Kingdom, this becomes a source of solace. When one turns to God, one finds spiritual sensibilities and forgets every grief and sorrow. Even if afflictions should assail from all directions, the heart finds comfort. When one turns to God, all this sadness, depression and gloom vanish, and the utmost joy and happiness are attained. Divine glad-tidings encompass such a one; in the depths of abasement, one finds glory; in utter poverty, one finds wealth.
selected.reason: Describes spiritual consolation amid the griefs of life.
